data.justification:
## Summary
openai/gpt-5-nano is the optimal choice for the NEAR dApp support agent, meeting all hard requirements at the lowest cost ($0.55 for the workload) while offering strong tool-calling, structured JSON output, and a 400k token context for long chat histories. Its pricing ($0.05/1M input, $0.4/1M output) undercuts all compliant alternatives, leaving budget headroom for scaling or error handling.

## Comparison
Among the 12 pre-filtered options, gpt-5-nano is the most cost-effective, with the next cheapest being gemini-2.5-flash-lite at $0.70 (27% higher). Higher-priced models like gpt-4.1-mini ($2.80) exceed the budget's value threshold without offering decisive capability gains for this use case—structured output and tool support are consistently implemented across candidates. While models like gemini-2.5-flash-lite and glm-5.3-flash offer larger contexts (1M+ tokens), gpt-5-nano's 400k context already exceeds the 200k requirement and is sufficient for extended chat histories; the cost savings outweigh the marginal benefit of extra context here.

## Recommendation
Select openai/gpt-5-nano. It delivers the best value for money by minimizing cost while reliably meeting the functional needs: it supports tools and structured_outputs, has a 400k token context, and processes the 3M input + 1M output token workload for only $0.55—well under the $3.00 budget. The model's reasoning feature (listed in its catalog entry) further enhances its suitability for a support agent that must interpret user queries, call tools like wallet lookups, and return precise JSON responses. Alternatives are either more expensive without proportional performance improvements or, like the Qwen models, have significantly higher output pricing that reduces value for this output-heavy workload.
